title: Choose the look for the Assigent start page
question: The roll assigned the school noticeboard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: School noticeboard
options.lineage: the corridor noticeboard every school has
options.thesis: Assigent pinned up as a circular in the corridor: the install line is a tear-off strip you take.
options.viewport: Full-width green board; one big 'NOTICE' circular pinned off-centre with the headline, its bottom cut into tear-off strips carrying the install command (tap a strip to copy). Agents pinned beside it as five coloured slips, numbered 1 to 5.
options.risk: Can turn into a cute scrapbook if pins and tape multiply; one board, few pins, real type.

raised.raise: Each slip explains one step with one small drawn diagram, not a paragraph.
A live 'Today on the board' strip shows a made-up run moving agent by agent.
Every agent slip is numbered and named in the same breath: 1 Analyst, 2 Source finder, 3 Builder, 4 Evaluator, 5 Tutor.
Every zone is labelled by its literal name, like a board header: NOTICE, RULES, HOW TO JOIN.

options.label: The exercise notebook
options.lineage: brown-paper covered school notebook with a name label
options.thesis: The page is your notebook: kraft cover with a name label, ruled pages inside where the agents work.
options.viewport: Kraft cover full-bleed with a white label: Name, Subject: Assignments, and the install command written on the 'Class' line.
options.risk: Close to the cream-paper look most runs land on; needs the kraft and blue ink to carry it.

options.label: Split-flap departures board
options.thesis: Your assignment departs through five platforms: each agent is a row that flips to DONE.
options.viewport: A black board with five rows (Analyst, Source finder, Builder, Evaluator, Tutor) flipping to DONE; the install line is the top row.
options.case: Strong on clarity: the pipeline reads instantly. Weaker on audience: it is a station, not a school.
options.risk: Becomes a costume if the flips run without meaning.

options.label: Hand-drawn explainer zine
options.lineage: a friend sketching it on a napkin
options.thesis: A friend explains Assigent in marker: arrows from the brief to five doodled helpers.
options.viewport: Marker headline, a doodled pipeline of five helpers with looping arrows, highlighter on the install line.
options.case: Teaches well and feels student-made; loses on audience because it reads as a comic, not school.
options.risk: Cream ground plus marker is a common look; can read childish to older students.

options.label: Alphabet storm
options.thesis: Letters of the brief storm into the finished work.
options.viewport: A brief's words dissolving and reforming as a finished page.
options.risk: Pretty, but hides what the product does.
options.case: Students do not see themselves in it, and the pipeline gets lost.
options.kept: Headline type set big enough to act as the page's structure.

options.label: Industrial quote labels
options.thesis: Every part named in straight quotes: "INSTALL", "AGENTS".
options.viewport: Big quoted caps over hazard stripes.
options.risk: Fashion pose with nothing to do with assignments.
options.case: Weak fit for students doing homework; clarity only from labels.
options.kept: Literal zone labels as the wayfinding.

options.label: Skate deck wall
options.thesis: Agents as decks on a wall, flipped to their art.
options.viewport: A rack of five tall decks.
options.kept: One full-height card per agent, browsed as a set.

options.label: Lotería night
options.thesis: Agents as numbered cards called one by one.
options.viewport: A called card above a four-by-four tabla.
options.risk: Culturally far from most students using it.
options.case: Audience does not know the game; clarity is indirect.
options.kept: Each item named and numbered in the same breath.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer-tool landing page, executed well.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, subline, install box with copy button, then a row of agent cards.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every CLI tool's page; nothing says school.
